title: Ordinary constant-module realization under normalized stratum transport
statement: Let T and S be schemes, g:S→T any morphism, l a prime and E/Q_l a finite extension. Let d be an adic datum on O_E with ideal generated by its recorded uniformizer, and c a normalized IntegralResidueCoefficientModel on S [lem-weil-pbc-integral-residue-coefficient-model]. Let B_T be the completed coefficient sheaf for pbcIntegralDatum l E and e=integralResidueStratumCoefficient [lem-weil-pbc-integral-residue-stratum-input]. The ordinary module functor integralConstantModule_T followed by the exact ringed inverse image along g and scalar restriction along e inverse is naturally isomorphic to koszulConstantFunctor_S followed by ordinary scalar extension along completedAdicScalar_S. The common domain is ModuleCat^(u+1)(ULift O_E), and the codomain is CompletedAdicModules S d. These are the actual constant sheafification and completed scalar realizations [def-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-models]; no complexes, perfectness, completeness, or covering assertion occurs.

proof.text: Construct the constant presheaf/evaluation adjunction explicitly at a terminal pro-etale object; the inverse sends a section at that object to all its restrictions. Compose with module sheafification to obtain the constant-module adjunction. Compose further with the fixed scalar-extension adjunction and the normalized coefficient equivalence to obtain the integralConstantModule adjunction.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.8(1),(2), Lemma 6.6.8 and Proposition 6.6.11; coefficient-presentation comparisons on constant sections and quotient projections.

proof.text: Compose the integral adjunction with the ringed inverse-image adjunction and restriction along the coefficient isomorphism. The resulting right adjoint evaluates modules at g*U for a terminal U over T. The right adjoint of the target realization evaluates at the same terminal object g*U. Their underlying abelian groups agree; the scalar-normalization equation makes their A-actions identical. Identity section maps therefore define a natural linear isomorphism of the right adjoints.

proof.text: Transport the left adjunction along that natural isomorphism and apply uniqueness of left adjoints. This yields the ordinary natural comparison without boundedness or projectivity assumptions.

lean.statement:
theorem integralResidueStratum_ordinary
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (g : S ⟶ T)
    (d : AdicCoefficientDatum (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E))
    (hd : d.ideal = Ideal.span {Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E})
    (c : IntegralResidueCoefficientModel l E d S) :
    Nonempty
      ((integralConstantModule T (pbcIntegralDatum l E) ⋙
          proEtaleRingModulePullback g (pbcAdicCompletion T (pbcIntegralDatum l E))
            ((adicTowerInverseImage g).obj (pbcAdicCompletion T (pbcIntegralDatum l E)))
            (Iso.refl _) ⋙
          pbcRestrict (integralResidueStratumCoefficient T l E S g d c).inv) ≅
        koszulConstantFunctor S (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E) ⋙
          completedAdicChange S (completedAdicScalar S d))
